result.summary:
The earlier run was already complete, so I did not recompute it. RESULTS.md was complete and every number traced to out/analysis.out, out/results.csv or results.json. I assessed the positive controls (PC1-PC3), the negative controls (NC1-NC3) and the predictions P1-P7 against the preregistration. The preregistration is untouched, and the SCRIPTS.sha256 check passes for all frozen scripts.

A second full run of run.sh in replicate/ reproduces results.csv, all table counts and results.json bit-identically. The only differences are wall-clock fields: the ms columns, timing.txt, env_date.txt and the Semaev per-solve timing lines.

All seven predictions held. The F_{p^2} route is slower per E-relation than direct Semaev decomposition. Over the 33 powered cells (of 36) the cost ratio rho_gen ranges from 53.3 to 2812, and the 99% interval lower end is at least 2 in every one. Mean j/m2 over all 235,155 relations is 0.442. The separation lemma has 0 violations in 1,965,600 odd-order decompositions. The even-order curves give 2860 violations in 655,200 decompositions, so both halves of P6 held. Semaev matches the table counts on 30 of 30 targets.

I added the operation-count metrics, which were missing, as derived arithmetic on recorded numbers only:
- e3_opcounts.gp (written after the run, not in the frozen hash set) and opcounts.sh write out/opcounts.csv, out/opcounts.json and out/semaev_ops.json, and merge them into results.json under op_counts.
- The script's work counts equal T*WD and T*WX of the frozen run in all 36 cells.
- Root-solves over the 33 powered cells: 93,000 for direct against 36,296,000 for the F_{p^2} route. Work (root-solves times degree): 258,800 against 662,348,800.
- Per E-relation, the F_{p^2} route over direct, powered cells: root-solves ratio 6.66 to 703, work ratio 53.3 to 2812 (equal to rho_gen), table sign-sum ratio 93.3 to 2031. All three are above 1 in every powered cell.
- Field multiplications and polynomial-evaluation counts were not instrumented in the frozen scripts, so they are not reported.

I also updated the following:
- run.sh now calls opcounts.sh as its last step.
- RESULTS.md has new Operation counts and Replication sections.
- DEVIATIONS.md has new items 7 (operation-count addendum) and 8 (replication).

Limits:
- This is a Semaev work-unit comparison on toy fields (p = 101 to 401, N up to 40, 200 targets per cell). It makes no rho or GAE claim and no improvement claim.
- 3 of 36 cells are unpowered.
- Semaev wall-time ratios are contention-affected. The X_4 over D_2 per-solve ratio was 61.6 to 119.5 in the original run, and 80.8, 77.9, 80.6 in the first replicate. It was 177.3, 97.9, 101.5 in the final replicate (load average about 14). All exceed the registered threshold of 4.
- The mental m=2 guess of 10^2 to 10^3 is confirmed only as a lower bound. Three powered cells (p=401 c1, N=16, 24, 32) exceed 10^3.
- The agent-delegation request could not be honoured: no subagent tool was available in this session, so I did the work directly, using only cheap derived computation and one roughly 2-minute gp rerun.

math.corrected_conclusion: The core conclusion survives my checks: on these toy cells the F_{p^2} eigen-decomposition route costs far more per E-relation than direct Semaev decomposition, with rho_gen from 53.3 to 2812 over 33 powered cells, and the group-law ground truth and headline operation totals are correct. I recomputed independently in gp: brute-force group-law counts for p=101 c1, N=16 match all 200 targets (D_2 168, X_4 431, j<=2 351; 0 per-target mismatches), and the root-solve totals (94,400 / 37,440,000 over all cells; 93,000 / 36,296,000 over powered cells) match. Three statements need correcting. (1) The D_2 root-solve counts for the three Semaev cells are 50, 70 and 30, not 2500, 3500 and 1500, which are inflated 50x by timing repeats; the matching X_4 counts are 2200, 5600 and 5600. (2) The opening claim "did not recompute" contradicts the replicate runs described in the same report. (3) Several "controls" cannot fail and should not count as evidence: P3, P5/H3, NC3, NC2 and H4 for odd-order curves. The headline claim stands as a toy-field work-unit comparison. The separation lemma is a one-line consequence of pi(S)=S (A-B = A+B gives 2B=O) and is not an empirical finding. The work unit also under-charges the X arm (F_{p^2} root-solves, resultant construction, 4x redundancy per set), so the error runs in the conservative direction.
issues: WRONG REPORTED NUMBER (RESULTS.md Operation counts, e3_opcounts / semaev_ops.json, out/semaev_summary.csv): 'D_2 root-solves 2500, 3500, 1500' is NE*TS*REPD with REPD=50 timing repeats (e3_semaev.gp sets Dsolves=NE*REPD per target). Actual root-solves for one run are NE*TS = 50, 70, 30 (NE=5,7,3; I recomputed NE from the curve parameters). X_4 root-solves 2200, 5600, 5600 are correct (C(N,3)*10). The X/D op-count ratio on the Semaev cells is therefore understated by 50x as reported. The per-solve microsecond figures are not affected, since time and solve count both include the repeats.

SELF-CONTRADICTORY PROVENANCE: the claim says 'the earlier run was already complete, so I did not recompute it', yet it also reports a second full run in replicate/ that reproduced results bit-identically, plus one ~2 min gp rerun. Which results were checked by recomputation is unclear.

CONTROLS THAT CANNOT FAIL, reported as passes without that caveat. P3 (rho_exact >= rho_gen) holds by construction, and RESULTS.md says so. P5/H3 ('every E-part is a direct D relation', 0 exceptions) is an identity: the X pass keys on the same E-subset sums, and the X = D_j*T_k check (fm) is also tautological. NC3 (E-only base, B nonzero, 0 hits) cannot fail, since all-E sums have zero twist part and B is drawn nonzero. NC2 redraws B from the same uniform distribution as the main arm, so the null is true by construction and it only detects gross coding bugs. H4/NC1 for odd order is a trivial theorem: pi(S)=S gives 2B=O, and B=O for odd order. The audit is a valid code check, and the 2860 even-order violations in P6 are meaningful, but none of these is independent evidence about cost.

DESIGN CAVEAT NOT STATED: H1 defines the target as A+B with B uniform nonzero. For a real ECDLP target R in E(F_q), B=O, and the lemma says the F_{p^2} route then yields only direct relations, so the route is vacuous for the actual DLP. The measured ratio therefore compares the cost of hitting (A,B) jointly with the cost of hitting A alone. This makes the product-of-probabilities result nearly inevitable, and it says nothing about the real attack.

BASELINE ASYMMETRY (conservative, not fatal): D_m counts only j=m E-terms exactly, while X 'generous' counts j=1..m. Work counts every (m-1) or (2m-1)-subset, so each set is found m times (D) or 2m times (X), which is redundancy that is not removed. The unit 'root-solves x degree' ignores that an X solve is over F_{p^2} with a per-tuple resultant. The measured X_4/D_2 per-solve time ratio of 61.6 to 119.5 against a degree ratio of 4 shows how large the under-charge is. This strengthens the direction of the conclusion, but rho is not a cost ratio in field operations.

WEAK TIMING / POWER: D_2 timing for the (101,12) cell is 6 ms total at 1 ms granularity (about 17% resolution), and per-solve ratios vary 61.6 to 177 across runs. The (211,16) PC2 cell has 1 relation in each arm, so PC2 equality there has almost no power. Field multiplications and polynomial evaluations are not instrumented, as the report itself admits.

Wrong number in RESULTS.md Operation counts: the Semaev PC2 D_2 root-solve counts are given as 2500, 3500, 1500 for 10 targets. In out/semaev.csv, Dsolves is 250, 350 and 150 per target, which equals N_E x REPD (5x50, 7x50, 3x50). The timing repeats (REPD=50 in e3_semaev.gp) are folded into the count. A single D_2 run uses N_E solves per target, so the true totals are 50, 70 and 30. The X_4 counts (2200, 5600, 5600) are single-run C(N,3) per target. The D-versus-X root-solve comparison for the Semaev cells is therefore inflated by 50x on the D side, and the figures in out/semaev_ops.json are likely affected too (not inspected).

The Semaev wall-time evidence for P7 (second half) is weak. D_2 timing is 1-ms-granularity batches (D_ms_per_solve_batch values of 0, 1 or 2 per 50 repeats), so the 2.4/4.6/6.0 us per solve figures are heavily quantized. X_4 is a single unrepeated run, so the two arms are timed asymmetrically. The ratio varies 61.6 to 177 across runs on a contended 4-core box, from 10 targets and 3 cells. It is far above the registered threshold of 4, so the verdict probably holds, but it is contention-affected and should be reported only as secondary. The report does say this.

The positive controls for the Semaev solver are low-powered. PC2 cell (211,16) has 1 D_2 relation and 1 X_4 relation in 10 targets. The (101,12) cell has 5 X_4 relations. Agreement on 30/30 targets mostly means agreement on zero counts. PC3 only validates the direct-arm model yield, not the X arm or the effect detector for the claimed gap. The effect itself is checked mainly through the even-order lemma audit (2860 violations) and the structural identity X = D_j x T_k.

The 'operation counts' addendum is not an independent measurement. The work ratio is identical to rho_gen by construction (root-solves x degree is the frozen unit). The group-sum counts are derived arithmetic. The script e3_opcounts.gp, run.sh and opcounts.sh are outside the SCRIPTS.sha256 freeze. Field multiplications and polynomial evaluations were not instrumented, so the primary cost metric requested (field multiplications / polynomial evaluations) is only partly met. The work unit also charges a degree-8 F_{p^2} solve the same as degree-8 F_p work, so real field-multiplication cost is not measured.

Scope is toy fields only (p=101..401, N<=40, 200 targets per cell, 3 of 36 cells unpowered). Several 99% bootstrap intervals rest on small D totals (about 20 to 170 relations). Nothing here supports a claim at cryptographic sizes or against rho. The hand-picked sizes, the mental m=2 guess and the p=401 c1 values above 10^3 only show growth with p over a tiny range. NC2 is a per-cell permutation test with only a null result, and no power analysis is given for it.

Minor process notes. The preregistration was written 2026-10-21 and the pre-freeze development runs on real grid cells were seen by the author. This is disclosed in DEVIATIONS.md but means the freeze is not fully blind. e3_lib.gp was written by an earlier session with no recorded test. The unpowered cells appear in the plots. The SCRIPTS.sha256 check passes for all frozen scripts.
stats.corrected_conclusion: The core claim holds. The F_{p^2} route costs 53.3x to 2812x more per E-relation than direct Semaev decomposition on the 33 powered toy cells (99% bootstrap lower end at least 27.3 in every cell). The separation lemma shows 0 violations on odd-order curves and 2860 on even-order curves. Mean j/m2 is 0.442. All of this traces to out/results.csv and out/lemma.out. The sha256 check on the frozen scripts passes, and the replicate reproduces the counts. The claim should be tightened in four places. (1) Correct the Semaev D_2 root-solve counts to 50, 70 and 30 per 10 targets (out/semaev.csv Dsolves includes the 50 timing repeats), and recheck semaev_ops.json. (2) Treat the wall-time ratios as quantized and contention-affected, from 3 cells and 10 targets, with D_2 batches only 0 to 2 ms. They are not evidence beyond 'well above 4'. (3) Note that the Semaev PC2 positive control is mostly agreement on zero counts, and that the operation-count work ratio is the same quantity as rho_gen, not an independent confirmation. (4) Limit the claim to toy fields (p up to 401, N up to 40, m = 2 and 3). It says nothing about cryptographic sizes, rho or GAE, and field multiplications were not measured.
